annotation.title_clean: South Africa's Artificial Intelligence (AI) Planning: Adoption of AI by Government
annotation.title_en: South Africa's Artificial Intelligence (AI) Planning: Adoption of AI by Government
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department of Communications and Digital Technologies (DCDT), South Africa; Mashishi, A.
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: October 2023 discussion draft of South Africa's national AI plan from the DCDT. It sets priorities in skills, investment, research and data, and proposes an AI Institute (AIISA) with hubs and a governance structure. It gives a regulation timeline for 2025–2027 and mentions autonomous devices only as a risk.
key_provisions_or_claims: Establish AIISA with AI hubs and an AI Expert Advisory Council under DCDT
National targets: 30% of workforce AI-literate, 20,000 AI specialists, 100-300 startups
Regulation timeline 2025-2027 covering AI applications, IP, competition and standards
Regulatory approach should be principle- and rights-based, globally aligned, and not stifle innovation
Lists risks from robotic or autonomous AI devices such as autonomous cars
